html:
The Arab conquest of the Maghreb began in 643, when Arab armies from Egypt took Barqa in Cyrenaica and then Tripoli. Over the next sixty years they pushed west to the Atlantic, ending Byzantine rule in North Africa.

The conquest was slow. The Berbers resisted hard, led by chiefs such as Kusaila and the woman known as al-Kahina. The general Uqba ibn Nafi founded Kairouan in Tunisia in 670 as a base. Carthage fell in 698, and by about 709 the whole coast was held.

Berber soldiers then led the invasion of Spain in 711, which created al-Andalus. Islam spread among the Berbers within a few generations, and Arabic slowly became the main language, sped up by the Banu Hilal later. See also the Arab conquests.
